title: api: standardize rate-limit/idempotency/retry-after semantics for streaming + openai-compat
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Streaming endpoints and the OpenAI-compat layer had diverging semantics for rate-limit headers, Retry-After responses, and idempotency enforcement. Clients observed missing X-RateLimit headers for chunked/streamed responses, inconsistent Retry-After behavior on transient throttles (429/503), and duplicate tool/function invocations when clients retried streaming requests without a stable idempotency key. This PR unifies rate-limit header semantics, makes Retry-After behavior deterministic, and applies idempotency consistently across streaming sessions while preserving OpenAI-compat payload shapes.

What this PR does: - Standardizes rate-limit headers across all API surfaces (hosted, openai-compat, streaming): X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset are emitted on initial response headers where possible and included in HTTP/1.1 trailers for chunked streaming. For HTTP/2 streaming we ensure equivalent initial meta frames are populated. - Retry-After handling: 429 and 503 responses include Retry-After (seconds) with consistent semantics. For streaming sessions we now send an immediate 429/503 with a Retry-After and close the stream; previously streaming handlers sometimes left half-closed channels leading to client ambiguity. - Idempotency keys: idempotency-key middleware now records a streaming request signature at session start and enforces single-execution semantics for server-side side-effects (tool calls, external webhooks). Retries by clients with the same Idempotency-Key will return the original result or an in-progress token, avoiding duplicate tool invocations. - Error shape & codes: standardize error body to include a top-level "code" aligned with OpenAI-compat strings (e.g., "rate_limit_exceeded", "server_error", "invalid_idempotency_key"). This is added without removing existing Redwood error fields to remain backwards-compatible. - Docs & SDKs: updates to docs/openai-compat and a minor note in redwood-sdk-js/ts usage examples to prefer idempotency keys for streaming calls that trigger side-effects. - Tests & canaries: unit tests for middleware, e2e streaming tests that assert headers/trailers, and a perf canary run to ensure no token-level latency regression.

Implementation notes: - Introduced streaming-aware RateLimitMiddleware that emits headers to both headers and trailers as supported by the connection. - Persisted idempotency records to the existing idempotency store with a new streaming state enum (PENDING, COMPLETED). PENDING allows other clients to receive a 202-in-progress envelope until completion to reduce busy-wait polling. - Kept OpenAI compatibility layer response shapes intact; compatibility tests added to prevent regressions. - Added a small compatibility shim in openai-compat/handlers to translate Redwood's internal error "code" -> OpenAI-style strings for older clients while encouraging clients to use canonical code.

Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind a runtime flag (api.unify_rate_limit_headers) initially enabled for Canary and Dedicated beta customers. - Monitor metrics: rate-limit header emission rate, idempotency-store hit-rate, duplicate-tool-invocation metric. - If stable after 72h on canary, enable for all hosted traffic and remove gate after two weeks.

Backward compatibility & migration: - Clients that previously inspected only initial headers will continue to work for non-streaming responses. For streaming clients that relied on trailers, the behavior is unchanged or improved; for older HTTP stacks that don't surface trailers, clients should read the first header delta sent by the server. - Idempotency changes are additive (prevents duplicates); clients that do not provide Idempotency-Key see no change. - Error body gains a "code" field — consumers should prefer this machine-readable field over relying on message strings.

Testing & CI: - Added unit tests for RateLimitMiddleware and Idempotency middleware. - Added integration/streaming-e2e which intentionally simulates throttling to assert Retry-After and proper stream closure. - Ran perf canary to validate no latency regressions in token p99.

Remaining work: - SDK helpers to expose streaming in-progress polling helper (follow-up: ENG-4389). - Expand canary to additional regions and Dedicated clusters.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration/e2e - [x] Docs - [x] Canaries/benchmarks - [x] Add migration notes

Related: ENG-4321 (rate limit unification), SUP-980 (customer-reported duplicate tool calls), ENG-4389 (SDK streaming helpers).

review_comments: Diego Ramos: please add an explicit unit test for the trailer emission on HTTP/1.1 chunked connections — done in tests/integration/streaming-e2e.test.ts

Marta Li: how do we handle idempotency-store growth for long-lived streaming requests? Author reply: we set a short default TTL for STREAMING:PENDING entries (configurable) and a compaction job cleans up orphaned PENDING states after 24h.
Jun Park: CI flaked once on integration e2e (timeout). Action: increased test timeout and added retry for transient network failure — CI passed on rerun.
release_notes: Standardized rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-*) across streaming and OpenAI-compat endpoints
Consistent Retry-After semantics for 429/503 on streaming requests
Idempotency keys now prevent duplicate tool/function invocations for streaming requests
Error responses include a machine-readable `code` field aligned with OpenAI compatibility
